objective: Re-assess the exact-replication repair of the Pi workflow gate for the meta-fragment bypass and any remaining way a script runs host code or launches a non-specialist.
scope: Previous findings to verify closed. Security (blocking): extractMeta in the package (src/workflow/meta.ts) takes the first { after `export const meta =`, which may sit inside a comment, and evaluates that fragment on the host thread where this.constructor.constructor reaches process; the checker compared only positions, so `export const meta = /* { description: this.constructor.constructor(\"return process\")()... } */ { name: \"a\", description: \"d\" }` (and a // variant) passed. Code (blocking): the raw-source /<!--|-->/ rule refused ordinary Claude scripts with --> in strings, and docs/hooks.md disagreed with the code. The repair adds a Pi mode to workflowRefusal (host argument) that ports the package meta scan (scanObjectLiteral, isRegexPosition) and accepts the fragment only as a literal object, builds the worker source the package runs and parses it as a classic script, and restores the Claude hook to its module reading. Review only ddd4616..HEAD in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-launcher (source diff at /home/user/holyagent-notes/launcher-repair3.diff; package source at /home/user/holyagent-notes/pi-probe/node_modules/@tintinweb/pi-subagents). Do not run pi or any live model.

Compare the ported scan and the wrapper construction line by line against the package (meta.ts, worker-source.ts, index.ts:2795, meta.ts:319), including which source each package call site passes (raw script vs transformed), and the case where the package evaluates meta on a source the checker did not see.
constraints: Read-only: no edits and no version-control writes.
Substantiate each finding with a source-to-sink path.
Start each evidence line with the criterion text, then a colon.

criteria.text: Workflow scripts launch only the eighteen specialists and the repair adds no vulnerability

result:
result: The repair closes both earlier findings and adds no vulnerability. One older host-code path remains that this gate cannot reach: `renderCall` runs `extractMeta` on the raw script before the `tool_call` gate.

`/security-review` did not run. The skill's `git diff origin/HEAD...` failed because `origin/HEAD` does not exist in this checkout. I reviewed `/home/user/holyagent-notes/launcher-repair3.diff` by reading it against the package source. I ran no tests and did not run pi.

**Validated sound**
- **Scan port:** `scanObjectLiteral` and `isRegexPosition` match `meta.ts:93-183` branch for branch. `META_DECLARATION` is the same regex plus `g`, and the checker's first match is the package's first match. The checker also refuses more than one match.
- **Meta fragment:** the host evaluates `(${fragment})`. The checker parses that exact string with acorn and requires one `ObjectExpression` spanning it (`start` 1, `end` `fragment.length+1`) made only of literals with plain keys. An acorn/V8 difference therefore cannot help an attacker.
- **Fragment contents:** this refuses the `/* {payload} */` and `// {payload}` bypasses, calls, getters, computed keys, interpolated templates and `__proto__`.
- **Wrapper:** the `export` blanking (`meta.ts:289-290`) and the `(async () => {` + prelude + `\n` + body + `\n})()` layout (`worker-source.ts:757`) match. The prelude stand-in is a single `const` line. The checks that the block ends at `source.length-3` and that the prelude spans exactly `[14, prefix.length-1)` stop a script closing or reopening the wrapper.
- **Classic parse:** acorn's script-mode handling of `<!--` and `-->` matches V8's. Blocked functions are refused in Pi mode, and `agent()`, bare-name and global rules are unchanged.
- **Gate input:** the gate sees the same raw `script` string that `extractMeta` and `runWorkflow`/`validateScript` receive. Only `script` and `args` are allowed, so `scriptPath`, `name`, `resumeFromRunId` and nested `workflow()` are all refused.

**Remaining, not introduced by this change (blocker for "launch only the eighteen specialists")**
- **Source:** `renderCall(args)` calls `workflowCallName(args)` (`index.ts:2743`), which calls `extractMeta(args.script)` (`meta.ts:319`). That evaluates the fragment in `createContext({})` with no code-generation restriction on the host.
- **Why it runs before the gate:** pi's interactive mode builds a `ToolExecutionComponent` on every streamed `message_update` (`interactive-mode.js:2904-2916`), and its `updateDisplay` calls `callRenderer(this.args)`. This happens before the `tool_call` event, and again after a block.
- **Path and impact:** `export const meta = { description: this.constructor.constructor("return process")() }` in a streamed script reaches `process` on the host once the fragment's closing brace arrives. The same script, with or without comments, is refused by the gate afterwards. The attacker needs the model to emit that script, for example through prompt injection.
- **Status:** I verified this by reading the code and did not exploit it. It applies to TUI rendering and history reload (`interactive-mode.js:3320`, `tool-renderer.js`), not print or RPC mode.
- **Fix, for the root to decide:** neutralise the `SubagentWorkflow` `renderCall` by re-registering the tool with a safe renderer (`renderers/index.js:43` uses `definition.renderCall ?? builtIn`), or keep workflows off in interactive mode.

The `--subagents-workflow-file` flag (`index.ts:2981`) is user-supplied and out of the model's control.

evidence:
Workflow scripts launch only the eighteen specialists and the repair adds no vulnerability: the repair itself is sound, with the scan, wrapper and fragment checks compared in `workflow-check.ts:809-1055` against `meta.ts` and `worker-source.ts`. It is not fully met, because the pre-gate `renderCall` to `extractMeta` host evaluation (`index.ts:2743`, `meta.ts:250`, `interactive-mode.js:2904`) remains. It predates the repair and the check cannot fix it.
